papers.title_en: Robust Watermarks Meet Backdoored Models: Evading Diffusion Semantic Watermarks via Stealthy Backdoor
papers.authors: Jinyuan Liu, Tianshuo Cong, Pei Li, Tianrui Wang, Xinlei He, Anyu Wang, Xiaoyun Wang
papers.evidence: 针对潜在扩散模型语义水印的后门攻击
papers.tldr: 语义水印依赖神经网络检测，存在后门攻击风险。GhostVAE在VAE编码器中植入隐蔽后门，通过功率谱正则化构造通用触发器，并用参数对齐目标训练。在三个水印方案和三个扩散模型上，良性图像检测率94.4%，触发攻击成功率94.6%，且能绕过17种防御。工作揭示语义水印系统安全漏洞，强调需端到端安全防护。
papers.abstract_en: Although semantic watermarking is considered a promising safeguard for images generated by Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs), the reliance of the watermark detection pipeline on neural networks introduces a critical yet underexplored backdoor attack surface. To systematically study this vulnerability, we propose GhostVAE to plant a stealthy backdoor into the encoder of Variational Autoencoder (VAE), enabling reliable evasion of watermark detection. GhostVAE operates in two stages: it first constructs a universal trigger via power spectrum regularization to improve the trigger robustness, and then trains a backdoored VAE encoder with a parameter-aligned objective. Through extensive evaluations across three state-of-the-art semantic watermarking schemes and three widely adopted LDMs, we show that GhostVAE preserves watermark detection performance on benign images (achieving an average true positive rate of 94.4%), while simultaneously enabling highly effective evasion under trigger activation (achieving an average attack success rate of 94.6%). Moreover, we comprehensively analyze seventeen representative defenses and demonstrate that GhostVAE remains stealthy across the input space, parameter space, and latent space. Our work fundamentally undermines the trustworthiness of semantic watermarking systems and highlights that secure deployment of semantic watermarks requires end-to-end security considerations, particularly for neural network components.

papers.title_en: Auditing Data Provenance in LLM Fine-tuning via Intrinsic Distributional Fingerprints
papers.authors: Zirui Huang, Yunlong Mao, Wei Tong, Tingting Wu, Xin Ge, Sheng Zhong
papers.evidence: 利用内部分布指纹审计生成模型未经授权的微调
papers.tldr: 定制大模型可能通过未授权微调侵犯数据知识产权，现有审计方法需要干预数据准备或训练过程，且易被改写和蒸馏等恶意混淆手段规避。本文提出后验审计框架DPA，基于一个关键洞察：模型为保持效用必须保留语义实质与词汇形式的交叉，以此作为内在分布指纹。通过无偏输出采样量化指纹并构造统计假设检验，可在黑盒与恶意场景下可靠判断数据是否被使用。在医疗和法律任务上的实验表明，DPA显著优于现有基线，对改写和知识蒸馏具有鲁棒性，并凸显了该指纹可同时用于审计与隐私攻击的双重用途。
papers.abstract_en: The proliferation of customized Large Language Models (LLMs) poses critical risks of Data Intellectual Property (Data IP) infringement via unauthorized fine-tuning on proprietary data. Existing audit techniques are limited, as they require intervention during data preparation or training and remain fragile under malicious obfuscations such as data paraphrasing and knowledge distillation.   We propose \textit{Distribution Provenance Audit (DPA)}, a post-hoc framework for auditing data IP infringement in LLM fine-tuning under black-box and malicious settings. DPA is grounded in a critical insight: regardless of fine-tuning tactics to evade provenance, the practical necessity of maintaining utility constrains the model to preserve the fundamental intersection of semantic substance and lexical form. Accordingly, DPA captures this persistent lexical-semantic intersection as intrinsic distributional fingerprints. The framework formulates the audit as a statistical hypothesis test, effectively quantifying these fingerprints via unbiased output sampling to reliably reject the null hypothesis of non-usage.   Extensive experiments on medical and legal fine-tuning tasks show that DPA consistently outperforms existing baselines, remaining robust against adversarial trainers employing paraphrasing and knowledge distillation. We further highlight a fundamental dual-use tension: the same high-fidelity distributional fingerprints enabling reliable auditing may also facilitate privacy attacks.
